At work, with the crew, I just can’t seem to keep everything straight anymore. Organizing the daily tasks, making sure everyone knows what they’re doing – it feels like my brain just jumps from one thing to another, and I lose my place. My wife's been on my case too, saying I never stop. Even when I'm watching TV, I'm pacing, or fiddling with something. It’s like there’s a motor running inside me that I can’t shut off. And I tend to just ramble on, explaining things over and over, or talking over people without meaning to. Sometimes, I swear I hear things, like faint whispers when no one's around, or catch glimpses of movement out of the corner of my eye that aren’t there. It's unsettling, and it makes it even harder to focus on what's real and what's not."
D001-D005_h001.question_a:

My desk, my truck – it’s a disaster zone, and I just can’t seem to get a handle on organizing anything. My wife is always on my case about it at home too, everything in disarray. I try to focus, but my mind just drifts off, sometimes I'm staring at a blueprint and the next thing I know, I'm thinking about what I need to fix on the house, or I'm distracted by some noise from down the street. It’s like my brain just doesn’t want to stick to one thing.

And I can’t sit still, not for a minute. I’m always pacing, tapping my foot, or just fidgeting. My crew even jokes that I’ve got a motor installed in me. I also find myself talking a mile a minute, jumping from one topic to another without really finishing a thought. It causes a lot of problems with communication. I've also been seeing things, hearing voices—it’s unsettling. But these focus and restlessness issues? Those have been with me my whole life, since I was a kid in school; long before any of these other… experiences started up. It's not like these new things made me lose my focus. My mind was always like this.

"I’m finding it tough to keep my head straight these days, Doc. My divorce a year ago really threw me for a loop, and since then, things have just gotten... foggier. I'll be sifting through case files, looking for proof, and suddenly realize I’ve spent twenty minutes staring at a blank wall, completely lost in my own thoughts. Details just slip through my fingers, and I end up making silly mistakes that a P.I. shouldn't.

And don't even get me started on losing things – my car keys, my phone, important evidence I was just holding. It’s like they sprout legs and walk away. Every little sound, a car horn outside, a siren in the distance, can completely derail my focus. I often find myself pacing my office, just this restless energy coursing through me, making it impossible to just sit still, even when I'm supposed to be unwinding. Trying to just chill out and watch TV? Forget about it. And waiting in line, or for a client to finally make up their mind? It feels like an eternity. Sometimes, when a case gets really intense, I start hearing whispers, or seeing shadows in my peripheral vision, feeling like I'm being watched. It throws me off, makes concentrating even harder."
D001-D005_h020.question_a:

I’ll make dumb mistakes, overlooking critical details because I’m already thinking three steps ahead, or maybe five steps sideways. My ex-wife always complained about it, even before we split. Said I was always losing things – keys, important documents for cases, even my phone sometimes. And being a PI, that’s a real problem. I’m always feeling this buzz, this need to be doing something, even when I *should* be still. Like in stakeouts, I have to constantly fidget; my leg bounces, or I’m tapping my fingers. I can’t just sit and quietly observe. Waiting for someone to show up or for a lead to pan out feels impossible. I’m always interrupting, too, jumping in before someone finishes their thought, especially if I think I know where they’re going.

This isn’t new. My teachers were calling my parents about my focus issues and restlessness way before middle school, probably when I was six or seven. Now, lately, I’ve been hearing things, whispers, and sometimes seeing shadows in my peripheral vision, and that’s unsettling. But those other problems, the inattention and the constant need to move, those have been a steady hum in the background my whole life, long before these new, strange experiences started cropping up."

Following through on instructions, even my own, has become a real struggle. I'll get halfway through something, and my mind just decides to wander, and I simply can't finish it. It's affecting my work, my marriage, everything.

Interrupting people has become a real problem too; it's like the words just burst out before I can stop them, cutting others off mid-sentence. And then there are these… moments. Sometimes, I hear whispers, faint voices that aren't there, or I see things, quick flashes in my peripheral vision that vanish when I turn my head. It's unsettling. This has been going on for a few months now, and I just can't seem to get a handle on it.
